text: Well, let's take a closer look at the strategy of a different sort of campaign. Up at the New York Senate race things are heating up, and last night was the first debate between Congressman Rick Lazio and Hillary Rodham Clinton, a debate that really defined the word debate, it got pretty contentious. Joining us from New York, two longtime political activists, Bill Dal Col is Rick Lazio's campaign manager. Mrs. Clinton's campaign manager is Bill de Blasio. And I welcome both of you to

speaker_label: EARLY EDITION. BILL DAL COL, CAMPAIGN MANAGER, LAZIO FOR SENATE CAMPAIGN
text: Thanks for having me on.
I'm going to assume for political expediency that you both believe that your candidates won last night's debate.
That's a safe assumption.

speaker_label: BILL DE BLASIO, CAMPAIGN MANAGER, HILLARY FOR SENATE CAMPAIGN
text: That's fair, that is very fair.

All right, well, let's start with you Mr. Dal Col. What I was wondering, in seeing some of the debate, why did Rick Lazio really make this race about Bill Clinton? Hillary Clinton didn't run for president.

Well, what you've got to look at it is Mrs. Clinton has no record, she's never voted for anything, never put any legislation in. She kept pointing to 30 years of work, which is interesting, but she failed to point out that most of it was in Arkansas. So what Rick had to do is demonstrate the fact that he's got a record, that he can provide leadership, that he'll be the senator from New York who will fight for the voters in New York. I think Rick did that, I think it was a lively debate. I think the voters got a look -- good look at both candidates and they can start to make up their mind now.
Well, what they saw was this dramatic moment where he decided to take this pledge and walk it over to Mrs. Clinton and ask her to pledge not to take any more soft money. Why the strategy behind that?

Well, what you've got a look at is Mrs. Clinton has run her campaign largely since June on soft money. There have been over 10 negative ads attacking Rick, distorting his record, paid for with soft money. She says she's for campaign finance reform, we've not set up any kind of a up to joint committee as she has, we've taken no soft money. It's time to put on the line. Can you trust her? Can you trust what she says? Will she do it she says? And I think answer clearly the voters of New York so far is no.
So Mr. de Blasio, why didn't she sign the pledge? What would be the harm?

Hillary made very clear last night she loved to come to an agreement, but as soon as Rick Lazio can guarantee that his many, many right-wing allies across the country will not continue vast expenditure campaigns on behalf of Lazio. You know right now $32 million has been pledged by groups around the country to support Lazio. As soon as he gets them in writing to say they're not going to do that, we'll be glad to move forward...
What do you think gentlemen?
A huge advantage, that's a huge advantage.

Well, I think you've got to look at all the outside groups that have helped Mrs. Clinton starting with the labor unions, let alone the power of the White House. We've seen this White House interject itself into the campaign. Hey, that's a tough mountain climb, we've got no outside groups helping us. Rick said he'd call for everybody to stop, just sign the pledge, there will be no soft money.

Well, Carol, the other issue here is that Rick Lazio had to resort to gimmicks because he spent the whole evening running away from his record. Here's a guy who voted against 100,000 new teachers, voted against school modernization, while working as Newt Gingrich's deputy whip, voted for the biggest education cuts in the history of the country. He didn't want to talk about his record last night. Bill Dal Col is absolutely right, Rick Lazio has a voting record, the interesting thing is how he avoids talking about it.

Carol, let's take a real look at it. The only candidate on that stage last night who has a record of accomplishment, voted to increase funding to the Department of Education, more than the president asked for, voted to increase funding to Head Start, more than the president asked for, voted for welfare reform. The president had to sign it after vetoing it twice. Rick Lazio has a real record, Mrs. Clinton at best is in New York for a visit. She didn't answer the big question last night, why New York and not Arkansas?

Well, let me ask you another question here. Let me ask another question here in the short time that we have left. There was an emotional moment there when Rick Lazio took Hillary Rodham Clinton on for what she said on the "Today" show about what she knew of her relationship with Monica Lewinsky. Mr. de Blasio, was she prepared to answer that question? She looked a little shaken by it.

Carol, she handled that question with incredible poise and dignity. And she got past that question and said now let's talk about today in New York, the issues confronting New Yorkers, let's talk about the need for jobs, let's talk about education and health care. Rick Lazio cannot afford for this race to really turned to the issues because when New Yorkers look at the questions of the issues, they know Hillary's on their side, and they know they can't count on Rick Lazio, his own voting record proves it.

Carol, let's also correct that. The person who took her on, on the Monica Lewinsky situation was Tim Russert. What Rick Lazio pointed out clearly, was that Mrs. Clinton can't be trusted because let's take a look at soft money. She said she wants campaign finance reform, but she wouldn't sign the pledge. Point to one piece of legislation that she has approved or voted for that helped anybody in New York. There is none. She has no legislative record, no experience, the biggest experience she can talk about is a failed '93 and '94 health care plan, and a record in Arkansas that they really don't want anybody to...

Carol, the other thing on soft money, ask Rick Lazio why he allowed the Republican Leadership Council to use Senator Moynihan's image in an inappropriate way, why he didn't stop that, why he denied knowledge of it. Let's get real about soft money.
Mr. de Blasio, I'm afraid I'm going to have to give Mr. de Blasio the last word on that.
Let's see if we can get Mrs. Clinton to tell the truth.
Thanks Carol.
You know let's see is can get both of them on EARLY EDITION and we'll talk to the candidates themselves. Thanks so much.
